newsitem.title: USA: StorMedia sees Q2 loss, cuts workforce.
newsitem.headline: StorMedia sees Q2 loss, cuts workforce.

text.p: StorMedia Inc said Tuesday it will report a loss for its second quarter and will cut its workforce by about 11 percent.

The computer disk maker said in a statement sales for the second quarter, ending June 27, will be well below analysts' expectations adding that it expects second quarter sales will approximate first quarter sales of $34.1 million.

The company said it expects to report a net loss for the quarter as a result of the lower revenues which it attributed to market conditions. The company did not specify what size of a loss it expected.
Analysts had expected the company to earn nil, according to First Call. The company had profits of $7.8 million, or $0.42 a share, in the comparable year-ago quarter.
The Santa Clara-based firm also said it will cut its workforce by 175 employees to bring costs in line with demand.
"This force reduction is intended to allow us to cope with recent demand softness without reducing our long term volume capability," Chairman and Chief Executive William Almon said.
